newsitem.title: USA: Colt's Manufacturing to acquire Belgian rival - report.
newsitem.headline: Colt's Manufacturing to acquire Belgian rival - report.

text.p: Gunmaker Colt's Manufacturing Co. will soon announce it is buying its chief competitor, Belgian gunmaker FN Herstal, from Giat Industries of France, the Hartford Courant reported Wednesday.
The newspaper, citing industry and U.S. congressional sources, said the announcement could come as early as Wednesday.
A Colt's spokeswoman declined to comment on the report.
Belgium's Walloon Regional Government, which owns an 8 percent stake in Herstal, had said it discussed a sale with representatives of Colt's Friday and planned further talks next week.
The acquisition would combine some of the world's best-known gun makers. Herstal owns the Browning and Winchester names, making weapons for civilian use.

Its FN unit supplies military hardware, including Colt's M16-A2 rifles and machine guns for the U.S. Army produced at a U.S. subsidiary. FN, formerly Fabrique Nationale, owns a factory in Columbia, S.C.
Giat, a French government-controlled defence company, announced in May that it was trying to sell the arms unit as part of a company restructuring.
It was not clear if Colt's would move its 635-person Connecticut operation out of the state if the deal goes through.
"It's a lot cheaper to work down there (in South Carolina) and produce than it is up here," defence analyst Gregory Fetter at Forecast International was quoted as saying in the newspaper report.
But congressional sources said a buyout could mean more jobs in Connecticut, depending on how it was structured.
